topic: How does congestion in feeder links impact spectrum management trade-offs for systems combining bent-pipe and digital processing?
consensus_response: Congestion in feeder links impacts spectrum management trade-offs by introducing interference between adjacent beams, reducing signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) and capacity. The high-gain antennas used in feeder links amplify both desired and undesired signals, exacerbating the issue. Digital channelizers can alleviate this problem but introduce complexity and costs associated with flexible channel allocation. Adaptive modulation techniques like adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) can help reduce interference by dynamically adjusting the modulation scheme based on channel conditions. Frequency reuse techniques, such as equal-cost multipath (ECMP), can increase capacity while minimizing interference.

It also discusses various approaches, including DVB-S2, ECMP, and RSVP-TE, which aim to optimize spectrum management trade-offs.
